Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Technologies Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star, then one on your telephone keypad. You will then hear an automated message advising your line is open. To withdraw your question, please press star, then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud Technologies's results for the Q2 FY2024. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Technology Officer; David Patel, Chief Product Officer; and Lisa Wong, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud Technologies delivered another strong Q2, marked by significant growth in our core cloud business and increasing adoption of our innovative AI solutions.

During the quarter, our priorities were focused on six key areas:
1. Expanding our global cloud infrastructure footprint.
2. Driving innovation in serverless computing.
3. Enhancing our cybersecurity offerings.
4. Strengthening our partnerships with leading ISVs.
5. Improving customer satisfaction and retention.
6. Investing in our talent pool and fostering a culture of innovation.

One of the brightest spots in our portfolio this quarter has been the explosive growth in AI and machine learning workloads, which now represents over 35% of our total revenue run-rate, up from 22% just a year ago. This isn't merely a passing trend—it's a structural shift reshaping the entire cloud computing landscape, and Nexara is positioned right at the epicenter.

The numbers really highlight the velocity of this adoption. In Q2, AI/ML workloads on our platform surged 162% year-over-year and 28% quarter-over-quarter, significantly outpacing our overall infrastructure growth of 41% YoY. To give you a sense of scale, we processed over 15 exabytes of AI training data last quarter alone—equivalent to streaming Netflix's entire global library 1,500 times. Customer adoption rates tell an equally compelling story: 72% of our new enterprise sign-ups included AI/ML components, compared to just 18% two years ago. This trajectory echoes the early days of the hyperscaler boom, but it's been supercharged by generative AI advancements like OpenAI's GPT-4o and Anthropic's Claude 3.5, which have made model deployment far more accessible.

By workload type, training continues to dominate, accounting for 58% of AI/ML compute hours, but inference is the fastest-growing area at 210% YoY growth. This momentum comes from real-time applications, such as RAG pipelines for customer service chatbots and multimodal inference for autonomous vehicles. Our Nexara AI Accelerators, powered by NVIDIA H100 and the upcoming Blackwell GPUs, achieved 95% utilization rates, with average instance runtimes stretching to 48 hours for large language model fine-tuning jobs. We've also witnessed a 340% ramp-up in vector database queries through our managed Pinecone-compatible service, Nexara VectorStore, as customers scale semantic search capabilities for enterprise knowledge graphs.

From a technical standpoint, our recent initiatives are delivering concrete outcomes. We launched Nexara ML Studio 2.0 in May, a fully managed end-to-end platform similar to AWS SageMaker but with seamless native integration for Hugging Face Transformers and Meta's Llama 3 ecosystem. Early adopters, including Fortune 500 leaders like AutoTech Innovations and HealthAI Corp, have reported 40% faster time-to-model deployment, slashing custom DevOps overhead through features like AutoML, Kubeflow orchestration, and our proprietary Nexara Tensor Optimizer for mixed-precision training. On capacity, we've scaled our AI-optimized zones to 250,000 H100-equivalent GPUs across 12 regions, with on-demand pricing starting at $3.50 per GPU-hour—highly competitive with Azure's NDv5 series while delivering 15% better FLOPS per dollar thanks to our custom interconnect fabric.

Regionally, the growth is diverse yet consistently strong. North America leads, contributing 62% of AI/ML revenue with 185% YoY growth, driven by Silicon Valley labs developing foundation models and Wall Street's quant trading algorithms. APAC has emerged as the breakout region at 220% YoY, spearheaded by hyperscale demand in Japan from workloads like Sony's image generation and in India from Reliance Jio's vernacular LLMs—though we've managed U.S. export controls by bolstering A100 stockpiles in Singapore. EMEA posted 140% YoY growth, with notable traction in Germany for industrial AI, where Siemens achieved a 5x speedup in predictive maintenance models on our Frankfurt zone, and in the UK for fintech fraud detection. Emerging markets like LATAM and MEA are early-stage but promising, showing 89% YoY growth linked to edge AI for telecoms such as Vivo in Brazil.

Strategically, we're cementing Nexara's role as the AI-native cloud leader. We've allocated $2.5 billion to AI infrastructure in FY24, including sovereign cloud expansions in the EU with GDPR-compliant zones featuring Homomorphic Encryption previews, and in Saudi Arabia to tap into Vision 2030's $20 billion AI investment. Sustainability remains core—our AI workloads operate on 68% renewable energy, offsetting the 2-3x higher PUE of GPU clusters compared to standard VMs, and we're piloting liquid-cooled data centers to accommodate Blackwell's 1,400W TDP. Partnerships are pivotal: our NVIDIA DGX Cloud integration and work with Mistral AI have secured multi-year commitments from 40% of the Fortune 100.

Forward-looking, we anticipate AI/ML workloads to expand 140-160% YoY in FY25, in line with IDC's projection of the global AI cloud market reaching $127 billion by 2027. Potential risks like GPU supply constraints should ease with NVIDIA's production ramps by Q4, while model commoditization is being addressed through vertical accelerators such as Nexara BioML for drug discovery, now in pilots with Pfizer.

In essence, AI/ML has become our primary growth engine, with adoption accelerating alongside capex cycles. We're not just riding this wave—we're engineering the tools to harness it.

Now I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a detailed review of our financial performance.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q2. Revenue increased by 42% year-over-year to $3.2 billion, driven by strong demand for our cloud services. Our gross margin was 74%, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency. Our operating margin was 32%.

Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. As your CFO, I'm excited to walk through our overall financial performance highlights for Q2 FY2024. This quarter showcased robust results, highlighting the resilience of our cloud platform amid surging demand for AI/ML workloads, hybrid multi-cloud strategies, and sustainable infrastructure. Let's break down the key figures.

On the top line, total revenue hit $3.2 billion, up 42% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter. This extends our streak of double-digit growth, surpassing the broader cloud market's 15-17% pace as noted by Gartner and Synergy Research. Core Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) led with 45% YoY growth to $1.9 billion, propelled by hyperscale GPU expansions for generative AI training—mirroring ramps at peers with specialized instances. Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) reached $900 million, up 38% YoY, powered by our Nexara AI suite where inference workloads jumped 45% QoQ as major financial services clients shifted from on-prem HPC. SaaS and data services contributed $400 million, growing 25% YoY, enhanced by edge integrations with partners akin to Akamai and Fastly.

Operating metrics further reinforce this momentum. Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) stands at $14.5 billion, up 46% YoY, with Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO) at $22 billion, rising 52% YoY for excellent multi-year visibility. Dollar-Based Net Retention Rate (NRR) is 118%, driven by expansions among our top 1,000 customers—who account for 65% of revenue and increased usage by 25% on average, especially in sovereign cloud setups. We onboarded 1,200 new customers sequentially, including 45 Fortune 500 wins in healthcare and automotive leveraging our confidential computing compliant with FedRAMP High and GDPR Tier 4.

Profitability remains a strength, with GAAP gross margin expanding 250 basis points YoY to 74.2% due to a richer compute-to-storage mix and our custom silicon—AetherCore v3 equivalents now yielding 30% better TCO than NVIDIA H100s. Non-GAAP operating margin rose to 32.1%, up 180 bps YoY, supported by disciplined CapEx at $1.1 billion or 34% of revenue, targeting AI builds in key regions. Free cash flow was $1.2 billion, up 25% YoY, fueling our share repurchase program and dividends.

By region, Americas drove 52% of revenue at $1.66 billion, up 44% YoY, boosted by U.S. federal deals under CMMC 2.0 and co-selling with Microsoft Azure Stack. EMEA added 28% or $896 million, growing 40% YoY despite German energy pressures—our 85% renewable-powered green data centers in Ireland and Sweden secured ESG wins with clients like Siemens and Unilever. APAC, at 20% or $640 million, accelerated 48% YoY via Tokyo and Mumbai expansions and Alibaba Cloud partnerships, capitalizing on India's $1 trillion cloud opportunity by 2030 per IDC.

These outcomes align with our pillars of AI ubiquity, sustainable scale, and ecosystem leadership. We've deployed $400 million this quarter in sovereign AI zones for Brazil and UAE, achieving 60% attach rates for NexaraGuard encryption. Liquid cooling has dropped PUE to 1.15 fleet-wide, meeting EU CSRD standards ahead of peers. Tailwinds from the $500 billion AI buildout through 2027 position us for market share gains in the $800 billion TAM.

Overall, Q2 confirms our execution, with raised full-year guidance to $13-14 billion revenue and 31-33% non-GAAP operating margin.

Next, I'd like to introduce Maria Chen, who will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Maria Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. On the technology front, we made significant progress in several areas. We successfully launched our next-generation Nexara Cloud platform, which offers enhanced performance and scalability.

Thank you, Jordan. Good afternoon, everyone. As we review our Q2 and full-year progress to date, I'd like to highlight our network performance and reliability metrics, the foundational elements of the Nexara Cloud platform. In an industry where downtime equates to millions in losses—around $9,000 per minute for Fortune 500 firms per Gartner—our SLAs and observability tools set us apart from hyperscalers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. We've upheld five-nines availability (99.999%) globally, with our UltraLowLatency tier at six nines (99.9999%).

Headline figures: Q2 global network availability reached 99.9992%, beating our SLA and improving 12 basis points QoQ from 99.9990%. Full-year to date, it's 99.9991%, up 18 basis points YoY from 99.9973%. This meant just 4.3 minutes of unplanned downtime monthly across our backbone—down from 6.2 minutes in Q2 last year. SLA credits were only $2.1 million, or 0.07% of revenue, far below industry norms of 0.2-0.5% seen in trackers like CloudHarmony.

Latency-wise, P99 end-to-end averaged 24.7 ms globally in Q2, a 15% YoY drop from 29.1 ms—outperforming AWS Direct Connect's 30-40 ms in cross-region flows and matching Google Cloud premiums. Peak throughput hit 12.5 Tbps during surges like Black Friday, with sustained averages at 4.2 Tbps via 400Gbps+ waves. Packet loss stayed at 0.007%—under 0.01%—and P99 jitter below 1 ms, ideal for real-time AI inference and AV pipelines.

Our AI-powered NexusGuard stack, using eBPF telemetry with Prometheus and Grafana, cut Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) to 2.1 minutes (from 3.8 YoY) and Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR) to 14.7 minutes (down 42% YoY). Anomaly models on 10 petabytes of daily data detect BGP flaps or DDoS precursors at 97% precision.

We've committed $450 million in CapEx this year to network upgrades, including 28 new PoPs for a total of 285 in 120+ cities—12 edge in Jakarta, São Paulo, Nairobi—reducing hops 22%. Our PathForge SDN with EVPN-VXLAN cuts failure convergence to under 50 ms, integrated with NVIDIA Spectrum-X for 51.2 Tbps AI fabrics. New undersea cables like Trans-Pacific Express 2 improved APAC-US latency 18%, and 100,000 km EMEA dark fiber supports 1.6 Tbps lambdas. NexusGuard 2.0 employs reinforcement learning for predictive scaling, plus post-quantum IPsec hardening.

Regionally: Americas (52% traffic) at 99.9995% availability, 18.2 ms P99—US-East peaked 8.9 Tbps. EMEA (28%) at 99.9990%, 26.1 ms, Frankfurt at 22 ms with DE-CIX peering. APAC (18%) 99.9987%, 32.4 ms improved 22% YoY via Singapore-Tokyo cable; China traffic up 60% YoY. Emerging at 99.998%, Mumbai 1.2 Tbps peaks.

These drive 92% retention vs. industry 85%, 37% premium attach rates. For FY24, we target 99.9994% with $600 million CapEx for 350 PoPs and 5G MEC. Risks like fiber cuts are offset by 2,500+ peering sessions.

Our network powers 42% YoY revenue growth—redefining cloud possibilities.

Now, I'll pass it over to David Patel for a product roadmap update.

David Patel:
Thank you, Maria. We are excited about the market reception to our new Nexara AI Accelerate offering. This product is designed to address the evolving needs of our customers in the AI/ML sector.

Thank you, Maria. Good morning, everyone—though it's afternoon now—and thank you for joining. I'm thrilled to discuss our new service launches and their exceptional market reception this quarter. As hyperscalers vie for share in a $200 billion+ cloud infrastructure market growing at 25% CAGR per Gartner, we've innovated aggressively, pulling ahead of AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

Leading is Nexara AI Accelerate, launched early July, a flagship for generative AI with auto-scaling inference via proprietary NexaraNeXt TPUs—third-gen tensor units for Llama 3 and Mistral. Integrated NVIDIA H100/A100 clusters with 800Gbps InfiniBand deliver 40% lower latency, 30% better TCO vs. AWS Inferentia/Google TPUs per TPCx-AI benchmarks.

Reception has been stellar: $85 million ARR in 90 days, 135% NRR. 320 enterprise wins, including a top-5 bank migrating 15,000 vCPUs from Azure OpenAI and an AV firm at <50ms edge latency. Zero-ETL with Snowflake/Databricks sped insights 4x. AI compute revenue up 280% YoY, exceeding IDC's 220%; RPO $420 million, +150% QoQ.

This fronts our AI race, with sovereign-compliant AI (GDPR, homomorphic encryption) at 45% attach rate, boosting ACV 22%. Targeting $500 million ARR by FY25 end via Hugging Face and Anthropic ties.

Next, NexaraEdge Fabric, mid-August launch for edge where 75% data generates by 2025 per Forrester. 5G-integrated compute, sub-10ms VPC across 1,200 PoPs, Kubernetes-native with KubeEdge/Open Horizon, eBPF zero-trust. Optimized for IoT/ML/video/AR/VR, 60% egress savings.

ARR $42 million, 180% MoM growth. Wins: telco consortium 5,000 nodes for 5G, retail giant 99.999% uptime vision. NPS 78 vs. industry 45. NA 55%, APAC 35% (Singapore/Tokyo), EMEA 10% accelerating post-Frankfurt.

Edge strategy for hybrid dominance vs. Akamai/Fastly; PaaS flexibility to 1M RPS. 25% IaaS cannibalization but 3x high-margin uplift; 15% revenue by Q4 FY25.

Finally, NexaraGreen CarbonZero, September sustainability service. 100% renewable regions, carbon APIs, PUE <1.1, offsets. Liquid-cooled ARM Graviton rivals cut emissions 50%.

$28 million ARR, 250 betas incl. Fortune 10 energy on 10PB Scope 3. 92% renewal, Europe 40% via Green Deal; 8% sustainable share per Synergy.

NA 60% new service revenue ($155M QoQ), APAC 25% +220% YoY, EMEA 15%, LatAm 5%. New services 18% Q2 revenue (from 7% YoY), 95% margins. 45 AZs, $2.5B FY24 CapEx. Multi-cloud via NexaraBridge (85% Terraform).

GPU supply tight (10% Blackwell delay hit), macro slowed SMB 15% but enterprise ACV +30%. R&D 22% revenue drives 32% growth.

These launches define cloud's golden age.

I'll now hand it over to Lisa Wong to discuss our marketing initiatives.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, David. We have been focused on driving brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly effective in reaching our target audience.

Thank you, David. Good afternoon, everyone. Before questions, I'd like to update on our top priority at Nexara Cloud: data breach prevention and incident response. With the cloud market over $600 billion in 2023—fueled by Fortune 500 multi-cloud shifts—threats rose 45% YoY in ransomware per Gartner/IDC, post-SolarWinds. We've achieved zero customer-impacting breaches for seven quarters, blocking 2.7 billion malicious events in Q2—up 28% QoQ.

Prevention via Zero Trust Architecture across 48 AZs/24 regions:

AI/ML SentinelAI on 15PB telemetry hits 99.97% true positives, neutralizing 1.4M lateral moves (+35% YoY) on IAM anomalies like APT41.

AES-256/post-quantum encryption, BYOK/CKS with Thales/Entrust HSMs—68% top customers, 42% fewer misconfigs per Prisma scans.

Native CWPP with Falco/Tetragon eBPF, Istio micro-segmentation—95% automated.

100% SOC 2/ISO 27001/FedRAMP High; phishing <0.8%, passkeys FIDO2.

$285M FY23 spend (12.5% R&D), +22% Forrester score vs. peers.

Incident response: GIRT 24/7 SOC (350 analysts Dublin/Singapore/Ashburn). MTTD 4.2 min (-18% YoY), MTTR 12.8 min (vs. IBM 212 days); 87% auto-quarantined via Cortex XSOAR.

Immutable WORM backups: RTO <4h, RPO <1min. 156 RCAs feed SentinelAI. 1h breach notification, Trust Portal 92% access.

Regional: EMEA GDPR Frankfurt/Paris block 15% more threats, +31% regulated. APAC Singapore/Tokyo hybrid Alibaba, 40% DDoS spike thwarted (2.5 Tbps Akamai). US FedRAMP $1.2B federal +55%.

Future: $400M confidential computing (SGX/SEV-SNP), QRCS Q3 vs. harvest-decrypt. CrowdStrike/Zscaler integrations for $80B security share.

NPS security 78 (vs. 62), 94% renewals, 27% ACV upsell. Proactive moat vs. 60% cloud misconfigs (Verizon DBIR).

Back to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Lisa. We are confident that our strong financial performance, innovative technology, and talented team will enable us to continue to deliver exceptional value to our customers and shareholders.

Thank you, Lisa. Good afternoon, everyone. Before guidance, a walkthrough of our compute and storage capacity utilization rates—a critical efficiency gauge signaling demand and discipline amid AI/cloud-native shifts.

Q2 overall utilization hit 87%, +450 bps QoQ from 82.5%, +1,200 bps YoY from 75%—top-tier vs. AWS/Azure mid-80s.

Compute: 84%. VMs 81%, containers 88%, serverless 92%. GPUs 76% (+ from 62% YoY) on H100/TensorCore for trillion-param models.

Storage: 91%. Object 93% (S3-like), block 89%, file 90%. Tiered 11 9s durability.

Seq: compute +320 bps AI inference +180% YoY; storage +280 bps archival. YoY: migrations +25% Fortune 500, GenAI GPUs x2, supply norm +15% racks.

Regions: Americas 90% (87% compute, coasts 92%). EMEA 85% (+600 bps, storage 94% GDPR). APAC 82% (Japan/Singapore 88% Arm 40% power save).

Initiatives: 2nd-gen Arm Neoverse 30% racks +25% perf/watt. ML auto-scaler -15% idle, 35% spot. 500 MW added PUE 1.18 liquid. Edge pilot 70%.

Validate demand-led in $300B+ capex mkt (Synergy). Integrated stack upsells 70% high-util to AI. Risks GPU/energy; renewables mitigate.

Q3 guide 88-90% overall, compute 85-87%. Supports $12-14B FY capex.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you wish to register for a question, please press star, then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter. On the AI/ML side, how sustainable is the 162% YoY growth given GPU constraints, and what's your visibility into FY25 ramp?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. Great question. The 162% growth is backed by multi-year commitments and our diversified supply— we've locked in H100/H200 allocations and our custom accelerators bridge gaps. Visibility is strong with $420 million RPO in AI services alone, and we see 140-160% FY25 growth aligned with market forecasts. Partnerships with NVIDIA and others give us confidence.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi, team. Impressive margins—can you talk about the drivers behind the gross margin expansion and any CapEx changes for H2?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Emily. The 250 bps GAAP expansion to 74.2% stems from compute mix, custom silicon efficiencies (30% TCO edge), and utilization gains. CapEx stays disciplined at 33-34% of revenue, focused high-ROI AI regions; no major changes for H2, but we're raising FY outlook to $12-14 billion supporting 88-90% utilization.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are committed to transparency and open communication with our investors.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
